key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation with neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection for robust HDPE joints by predicting temperatures, axial forces and defect formation.
method: Simulate heat, material flow and defects using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force data.
Combine simulation and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free welding conditions.
evidence_signal: The experimentally validated CEL model reproduced thermal, mechanical and void-formation behavior; ANNs achieved R² of 0.91–0.99, while 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N.
watch_item: ANN accuracy is demonstrated within the tested parameter space; performance for other geometries, HDPE grades or operating conditions requires validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
